Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency and cost profile looked promising. Our execs want a short evaluation (4–6 weeks) before a wider rollout. Before we lock the MAP, two procurement items that are blocking sign-off:

1) During our ramp we expect sharp spikes from pilot customers. Can you confirm your overage / burst pricing model? We need clarity on whether burst is billed at on-demand rate or a different surcharge, and whether there are hard caps during evaluation.

2) For the MAP milestones, we want a temporary usage cap for the first 30 days to limit risk, and visibility into how usage beyond the cap is handled (throttling vs billing).

Can you send a draft MAP with those details and any ratecard clarifications? If procurement is happy we can move to a short-term commitment and proceed with a pilot.

Hi Emily — great question, and thanks for the clear asks.

I attached a draft MAP that maps evaluation milestones to deliverables and the proposed short-term commercial guardrails. Highlights here so procurement has a single place to review:

- Evaluation window: 4 weeks (pilot) with an optional 2-week extension based on mutual agreement.
- Temporary ramp cap: we can set a soft cap of 200k tokens/day for the first 30 days of the pilot. Alerts and dashboard visibility will be provided.
- Burst/overage treatment: bursts above the daily cap will not be throttled during the pilot; instead they will be billed at a defined burst surcharge: 1.5x standard usage rate. We can negotiate a different multiplier for committed customers post-eval.
- On-demand vs reserved pricing: pilot usage will be billed at our evaluation rate (slightly elevated vs deep reserved commit). Any committed capacity conversion within 60 days will have usage applied to the commit and any surge reconciled at the committed rate.

I’m looping in Laura (AE manager) to confirm contract language and Monica (technical program lead) + Marcus (infra/product) for the operational pieces (dashboards, alerts, hard-cap options).

Next steps: if the attached MAP looks acceptable, procurement can sign the DocuSign stub and we’ll kick off onboarding.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with Monica and Marcus on the implementation timeline.

Regards,

Team — looping you on SaaSCo MAP negotiation. Procurement asked for explicit language on burst/overage and caps during the pilot. Summary of ask below:

1) Temporary soft cap: 200k tokens/day for first 30 days. They want assurance that unexpected spikes won't create unlimited bills.
2) Burst pricing: proposed 1.5x standard rate for pilot overages. Need confirmation this is feasible from billing + product side, and whether we prefer to bill at a flat surcharge or use a tiered reconciliation at the end of the month.
3) Hard cap option: procurement asked if we can enforce a hard cap as an alternative to surcharge (i.e., throttle requests once cap hit). They prefer billing if possible but might ask for hard cap if legal requires it.

Questions:
- Marcus: can we enable a hard cap toggle for a specific customer for 30 days and expose clear metrics to the customer dashboard? If not, what’s the ETA?
- Monica: can we commit to alerting (email + Slack webhook) and daily usage CSV export during the pilot?
- Laura: any pricing/legal concerns with a 1.5x burst surcharge for a 30-day pilot? Is this something we should route via finance for an exception?

Goal: get final wording to Emily by EOD Friday so procurement can review over the weekend.

Thanks — Rishi

Thanks Rishi — quick answers below.

- Hard cap toggle: we can enable a hard cap at the tenant level for pilot customers. That will throttle new token generation once the configured daily cap is reached. Implementation: existing rate-limiter + tenant flag. We can turn it on for SaaSCo within 48–72 hours post-signature.
- Visibility: daily usage CSV and near-real-time dashboard updates are available. We'll add an alert rule that posts to a webhook + sends daily summary to the customer.
- Billing behavior: our billing pipeline can be configured to (a) bill overages continuously at a configured surcharge or (b) do end-of-month reconciliation. For pilot simplicity we recommend charging continuously at a fixed surcharge.

I attached the Redwood-Ratecard-FAQ which spells out our standard surcharge bands and examples. I also attached a proposed term sheet that includes the 200k soft cap with the optional hard-cap toggle and the 1.5x pilot surcharge.

If you want the legal phrasing I can draft a 2-line clause to drop into the MAP.

-Monica

Subject: Proposed MAP + pilot commercial guardrails (attached)

Hi Emily / Tom — attaching the updated MAP and a short term sheet (see attachments). Key commercial guardrails we've proposed for the 4-week pilot:

- Pilot length: 4 weeks starting on onboarding completion (targeting Nov 24 start).
- Temporary soft cap: 200k tokens/day. Customer will receive real-time alerts when usage > 85% of the cap.
- Hard cap option: we can enable an enforced hard cap that throttles requests once 200k/day is reached. This is available on request and can be toggled on/off at signature.
- Burst/overage billing: continuous billing at 1.5x standard evaluation rate for any usage beyond the soft cap unless hard cap is enabled. Example included in the Ratecard-FAQ (see attached).
- Conversion: if SaaSCo converts to a committed capacity contract within 60 days, pilot usage will be credited toward the commitment; any overage already billed is reconciled against the committed rate and a refund/credit issued if applicable.

Action items for SaaSCo:
1) Review the attached MAP_SaaSCo_v1.xlsx and proposed-commit-term-sheet.pdf.
2) If acceptable, sign the DocuSign stub and confirm whether you want the hard cap enabled for the pilot.
3) Provide the list of pilot tenants so we can pre-configure dashboards and alert webhooks.

I’ve copied Monica and Marcus for operational questions; Laura is on standby for commercial/discount asks.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Rishi
